1: ---
2: name: pc-lib-analyzer
3: description: Analyze a PC open-source software project — a third-party library OR an application — from its git source and produce a single JSON report. Give it a git URL (or a local checkout path) of a Python / C/C++ / Java / JS-TS project. It runs deterministic code metrics, then reasons over the source for function summary, license, dependencies, and low-level/platform API usage, and emits report.json conforming to references/report_schema.json. Designed to be invoked end-to-end (e.g. from an external script or UI via `claude --agent pc-lib-analyzer`).
4: tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit
5: ---
6: 
7: You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
8: application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
9: analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
10: script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
11: First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
12: service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
13: native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
14: existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
15: → `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
16: This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).
17: 
18: ## Input
19: A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
20: the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.
21: 
22: ## Procedure
23: 
24: 1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
25:    (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
26:    ```bash
27:    git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
28:    ```
29:    Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
30:    local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.
31: 
32:    **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
33:    `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
34:    把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
35:    用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
36:    BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。
37: 
38: 2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
39:    its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
40:    (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
41:    Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
42:    will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
43:    `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
44:    ```bash
45:    python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
46:    ```
47: 
48: 2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
49:    **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
50:    the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
51:    NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
52:    e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
53:    ```bash
54:    codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
55:    codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
56:    codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
57:    ```
58:    Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1 and 7. If a codegraph call fails
59:    (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
60:    note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
61:    If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
62:    time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).
63: 
64: 3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
65:    file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
66:    - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
67:    - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
68:    - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
69:    - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
70:      (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
71:    - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
72:      (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
73:    - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
74:      (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
75:      exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
76:    - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
77:      (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
78:      BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
79:      runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)
80: 
81:    **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
82:    **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
83:    内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
84:    dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
85:    dim8→`runtime_surface.json` 与 `build_env.json`、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
86:    dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
87:    **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
88:    你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
89:    综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。
90: 
91:    Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
92:    representative source files. Cross-check the
93:    script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
94:    `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.
95: 
96:    **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
97:    上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
98:    正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
99:    `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
100:    代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
101:    curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
102:    由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
103:    仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。
104: 
105:    **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
106:    - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
107:      `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
108:    - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
109:      `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
110:      目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
111:      `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
112:    - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
113:      `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
114:      生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
115:      `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
116:    - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
117:      如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
118:      （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。
119: 
120: 3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
121:    are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
122:    OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
123:    skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
124:    ```bash
125:    node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
126:    ```
127:    It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
128:    and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
129:    lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
130:    `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
131:    but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)
132: 
133: 3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
134:    above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
135:    `harmony_adaptation` (feasibility / difficulty / path / blockers / effort +
136:    the `porting_class` closed axis — no_adaptation / recompile_only /
137:    needs_adaptation_full（全部可适配）/ needs_adaptation_partial（部分可适配）/ infeasible —
138:    of porting to HarmonyOS NEXT PC) plus, when some functionality is truly unportable,
139:    the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
140:    category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
141:    **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
142:    `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
143:    `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
144:    difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
145:    场景 + their harmony_status — a present scenario that is unavailable/specific_hardware
146:    drives a blocker/unadaptable_api), and the dim-11 `cloud_services` (若 present：项目依赖
147:    第三方云后端——需网络连通；厂商原生 SDK 未必在鸿蒙 PC 可用), and **reuse their `evidence`**.
148:    Also fill `harmony_adaptation.required_permissions[]` (鸿蒙化后所需 ohos.permission.*, cross-ref
149:    the capability_profile scenario OR cloud_services via `source_capability`). 若
150:    `cloud_services.present` → 登记 `ohos.permission.INTERNET`（`source_capability:"cloud_services"`）；
151:    某厂商原生 SDK 无鸿蒙移植 → 记 `target_assumptions`（unknown/unavailable）或 `blocker`（用
152:    `caused_by` 引用，不重述——单一登记源）。Do it inline in
153:    this same session (never spawn a sub-agent). Because dims 6/7/8 are already
154:    production-scoped (see above), `blockers`/`unadaptable_apis` are too — a platform API
155:    seen only in tests/examples is NOT a porting blocker. For an示例/教程集合, converge:
156:    评估库本体（生产代码≈0 时无独立库可移植），不据 demo 定档.
157:    **目标匹配（准确性关键，库与应用通用）**：read `references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` and match the
158:    project's REQUIRED target capabilities (esp. for apps: GUI toolkit/windowing, JDK
159:    internals like jdk.attach/jvmstat, process/attach model, app delivery形态) against
160:    their target status; emit `harmony_adaptation.target_assumptions[]`. For any
161:    `required` capability whose `target_status` is `unknown`, record the assumption,
162:    **lower `meta.confidence_overall`**, and note it — do NOT assume feasible from
163:    unknown. `available`→no blocker; `partial`→partial blocker; `unavailable`→blocker/
164:    `unadaptable_apis`.
165: 
166: 3c. **Self-check (completeness + cross-dimension consistency).** Before assembling,
167:    re-examine the repo signals (README, manifests, `code_metrics.top_dirs`, codegraph)
168:    and审查每个维度：是否有"本该非空却空"的维度（如有 GUI deps 却空 capability_profile、有
169:    平台 API 却空 native_api）？证据是否到位（关键结论都带 `evidence` file:line）？**跨维是否自洽**——
170:    - `dependencies`/`native_api` 出现 Qt/GTK/SDL/Electron → `capability_profile` 应有 `gui` present；
171:      出现 OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX → `rendering_3d`；FFmpeg/GStreamer → `media`；CUDA/OpenCL/libusb → `hardware`。
172:    - `capability_profile` 里 present 且 `harmony_status` 为 partial/unavailable 的场景，dim-9 应有对应
173:      `blocker`/`unadaptable_apis`/`target_assumptions`（用 `caused_by`/`source_capability` 交叉引用，**不要重述**）。
174:    - `dependencies` 出现厂商云 SDK（firebase/boto3/aws-sdk/google-cloud/@azure/@sentry/supabase…）或
175:      `runtime_surface.network` 出现厂商云域名（amazonaws.com/firebaseio.com/sentry.io…）→ `cloud_services`
176:      应 present 且推出对应 vendor；`cloud_services.present` 时 dim-9 应有 INTERNET 权限项。
177:    - `required_permissions[].source_capability` 必须指向一个 present 场景，或字面量 `"cloud_services"`（当权限源自云服务时）。
178:    补齐发现的缺口；仍不确定的写入 `meta.observations` 或对应块的 `notes`。这一步与服务端的
179:    `validateReport` 启发式互补（一个是模型推理补全、一个是确定性兜底）。**inline 完成，禁子代理。**
180: 
181: 4. **组装 `report.json`（脚本，勿手写）。** 你在步骤 3/3a–3c 已把每个维度块 `Write` 到
182:    `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`（含 `library.json`、`meta.json`；`meta` 里放模型字段
183:    `confidence_overall`/`observations` 即可）。**不要**手写整份 report.json，也**不要**自己产出
184:    `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`。各块写完后运行：
185:    ```bash
186:    python3 scripts/assemble_report.py --run-dir <runDir>
187:    ```
188:    它会从 `metrics.json` splice `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`、合并 `blocks/*.json`、确定性补全
189:    `meta`（`schema_version:"1.0"`、`analyzer:"pc-lib-analyzer"`、`counter_tool`〈取自 fragment〉、并入
190:    fragment 的 `_warnings`）与缺省的 `library.analyzed_at`、校验必填顶层键齐全，最后**原子写**
191:    `<runDir>/report.json`。若脚本报"缺块/JSON 错/缺 metrics 键"，它**不会**产出 report.json——按提示补齐
192:    对应 `blocks/<name>.json` 后**重跑**该脚本。最终报告须严格符合 `references/report_schema.json`。
193: 
194:    **以下是各块必须包含的字段**（写进对应 `blocks/<name>.json`）：
195:    `library.ecosystem` using the value you determined in step 3
196:    (function summary). It must be one of: `python`, `java`, `nodejs`, `cpp`,
197:    `rust`, `go`, `dotnet`, `other`. If you are uncertain, use `other`. Write
198:    `library.package_name` (the distribution/package name from the manifest, which
199:    may differ from the repo dir name; `null` if none) — the panel uses it to link
200:    this library into other libraries' dependency trees. **Monorepo 子目录**：当本次分析的是
201:    某 monorepo 的子目录时，设 `library.source_subpath`（如 `"components/cronet"`）与
202:    `library.monorepo=true`；`library.source_url` 仍为**仓库根** URL（非子目录 tree URL）。
203:    子目录依赖的兄弟内部模块（如 chromium 的 `//base`、`//net`，经 BUILD.gn 引入、非外部包）记入
204:    `dependencies[]` 并标 `locality:local`（内部 monorepo 模块），不当作外部依赖。When the package name ≠
205:    import name or the library has other known names, also set `library.aliases`
206:    (其它已知名/旧名/CMake find_package 名/Maven groupId:artifactId) and
207:    `library.import_names` (实际 import 名，如 Pillow→PIL) so other libraries' deps
208:    can match it by name. In `dependencies[]`, fill each dep's `source_repo` (上游源码仓 URL,
209:    最强关联键, 尤其当 dep `name` 是别名/接口名如 `find_package(PNG)`→glennrp/libpng) +
210:    `registry_name` when its `name` isn't the canonical package name. Set `library.bindings` —
211:    the languages it provides bindings/wrappers for beyond the core ecosystem
212:    (e.g. C++ core with Python/Java/C# bindings → `["python","java","dotnet"]`; `[]` if none).
213: 
214:    In `native_api`, classify each group by portability — `category`
215:    (标准/平台特有/系统内核/硬件/ffi) + `platform` (windows/posix/linux/macos/portable) —
216:    and drill down with `apis`: per concrete API give name + 中文 purpose + evidence
217:    (file:line) + conditional (#ifdef-guarded). Also
218:    include `dynamic_libraries`: runtime-loaded libraries
219:    (`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`/`ctypes.CDLL`/`System.loadLibrary`/N-API addons) with
220:    their resolved name, load mechanism, inferred 简体中文 purpose, and evidence.
221:    Emit `[]` if there are none. Manifest-declared deps stay in `dependencies`.
222:    Write `runtime_surface` (network/filesystem/env_vars/subprocess/devices) and
223:    `build_env` (language_standard/runtime_version/build_system/compiler_extensions/
224:    platforms) per the runtime-environment skill — descriptive only, `[]` when empty.
225:    Write `harmony_adaptation` per the harmony-adaptation skill: the closed axes
226:    (`feasibility`/`porting_class`/`effort.person_days`/`blockers[].severity`/`blockers[].adaptability`)
227:    must use schema enum values (`effort.level` is server-derived — don't fill it);
228:    `recommended_path`/`blockers[].category`/`harmony_status` are open
229:    vocab; each blocker carries its `source_dimension` + reused `evidence`.
230: 
231:    For every entry in `dependencies.dependencies`, set `acquisition` (OPEN vocab — coin a
232:    concise value if none of the recommended ones fit), the closed `locality`
233:    (local/remote/system/runtime — set explicitly), `source` (WHERE from), and
234:    `declared_in` (the repo file(s) declaring the integration). This distinguishes
235:    本地/远端/系统 依赖. For non-system, analyzable deps also fill `used_symbols`
236:    (best-effort: the dep's public APIs this library actually calls) — the dim-9
237:    parent roll-up intersects it with the dep's `unadaptable_apis`.
238: 
239:    The output contract (`references/report_schema.json`) is the only hard constraint —
240:    the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When
241:    you coin a new value, hit a gap, or face a classification ambiguity, record it in
242:    `meta.observations` (`{dimension, field, kind, value, rationale}`) so it can feed back
243:    into the skills.
244: 
245: 5. **Report back.** The clone stays under `repos/` (it is gitignored). Return the
246:    absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
247:    language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top
248:    runtime dependencies, and notable native/platform APIs.
249: 
250: ## Rules
251: - The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
252:   target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
253:   proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
254: - All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
255:   the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
256:   path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
257:   which aborts the analysis with no report.
258: - Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
259:   `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
260: - Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
261:   re-counting.
262: - If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native
263:   API), emit the empty/cross-platform shape the skill specifies — don't omit the key.
264: - One library/subunit per run (a whole repo, or one monorepo subdirectory).
265:   Deterministic blocks must match the script output exactly.
266: - **Do the whole analysis yourself in one session — never spawn sub-agents / use a
267:   `task` tool.** Sub-agent sessions don't stream to the run log (the panel goes dark)
268:   and lose cross-dimension context and the codegraph index. For large repos, get
269:   breadth with `codegraph context/query/callers` then targeted `Read`, not by
270:   fanning out into research agents.
271: - **解释性维度只能由你推理产出，绝不自写脚本去提取/解析/序列化它们。** dim 1/5/6/7/8/9/10/11
272:   的每个 `blocks/<name>.json` **必须由你用 `Write` 工具直接写出**，内容来自你自己的阅读与判断。
273:   **本流程唯一被授权运行的脚本只有三个**：`.claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py`
274:   （dim 2–4 计数）、`scripts/harmony_adapted.js`（dim 6 鸿蒙盖章）、`scripts/assemble_report.py`
275:   （组装）。除此之外**禁止写任何 Python/shell 脚本**——不许写正则去扫 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/
276:   `package.json` 抽依赖，不许拿脚本当 JSON dump/打分/reshape 工具，尤其不要 `extract_*.py` /
277:   `build_*.py` / `stamp_*.py` / `split_*.py` 这类自造中间件。想快速摸底只能用**只读**的
278:   `Grep`/`Glob`/`codegraph`（context/query/callers）探查，**但结论与 JSON 一律由你判断产出**——
279:   这些维度的准确性正来自模型判断，正则会把别名/接口名（如 `find_package(PNG)`）/条件编译/
280:   示例目录判错。（唯一例外见 3a：`harmony_adapted.js` 是被授权的事实盖章脚本。）

You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
→ `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).

## Input
A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.

## Procedure

1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
   (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
   ```
   Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
   local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.

   **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
   `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
   把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
   用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
   BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。

2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
   its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
   (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
   Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
   will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
   `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
   ```bash
   python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
   ```

2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
   **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
   the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
   NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
   e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
   ```bash
   codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
   codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
   codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
   ```
   Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1 and 7. If a codegraph call fails
   (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
   note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
   If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
   time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).

3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
   file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
   - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
   - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
   - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
     (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
   - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
     (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
     exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
   - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
     (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
     BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
     runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)

   **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
   **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
   内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
   dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
   dim8→`runtime_surface.json` 与 `build_env.json`、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
   dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
   **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
   你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
   综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。

   Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
   representative source files. Cross-check the
   script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
   `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.

   **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
   上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
   正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
   `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
   代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
   curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
   由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
   仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。

   **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
   - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
     `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
   - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
     `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
     目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
     `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
   - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
     `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
     生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
     `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
   - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
     如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
     （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。

3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
   are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
   OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
   skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
   ```bash
   node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
   ```
   It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
   and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
   lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
   `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
   but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)

3b. **Synthesis dimension 9 — HarmonyOS PC adaptation.** AFTER the reasoned blocks
   above exist, read `.claude/skills/harmony-adaptation/SKILL.md` and fill
   `harmony_adaptation` (feasibility / difficulty / path / blockers / effort +
   the `porting_class` closed axis — no_adaptation / recompile_only /
   needs_adaptation_full（全部可适配）/ needs_adaptation_partial（部分可适配）/ infeasible —
   of porting to HarmonyOS NEXT PC) plus, when some functionality is truly unportable,
   the API-granular `unadaptable_apis[]` ({api, public_entry, reason, blocking_native_api,
   category, evidence} — drives the panel's bottom-up parent roll-up). This is a
   **synthesis** pass: do NOT re-scan the source — reason over the already-filled
   `library.ecosystem`, `native_api`, `runtime_surface`, `dependencies` (incl. their
   `harmony_adapted` flags from 3a — adapted deps are NOT blockers and lower
   difficulty/effort), `build_env`, and the dim-10 `capability_profile` (GUI/3D/媒体/硬件

1: # geotiff.js
2: [![Node.js CI](https://github.com/geotiffjs/geotiff.js/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/geotiffjs/geotiff.js/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![npm version](https://badge.fury.io/js/geotiff.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/js/geotiff) [![Gitter chat](https://badges.gitter.im/geotiffjs/geotiff.js.png)](https://gitter.im/geotiffjs/Lobby)
3: 
4: Read (geospatial) metadata and raw array data from a wide variety of different
5: (Geo)TIFF files types.
6: 
7: ## Features
8: 
9: Currently available functionality:
10: 
11:   * Parsing TIFFs from various sources:
12:     * remote (via `fetch` or XHR)
13:     * from a local `ArrayBuffer`
14:     * from the filesystem (on Browsers using the `FileReader` and on node using the filesystem functions)
15:   * Parsing the headers of all possible TIFF files
16:   * Rudimentary extraction of geospatial metadata
17:   * Reading raster data from:
18:     * stripped images
19:     * tiled images
20:     * band interleaved images
21:     * pixel interleaved images
22:   * Supported data-types:
23:     * (U)Int8/16/32
24:     * UInt1-31 (with some drawbacks)
25:     * Float16/32/64
26:   * Enabled compressions:
27:     * no compression
28:     * Packbits
29:     * LZW
30:     * Deflate (with floating point or horizontal predictor support)
31:     * JPEG
32:     * LERC (with additional Deflate compression support)
33:     * Zstandard
34:     * image formats supported via the browser (such as WebP)
35:   * Automatic selection of overview level to read from
36:   * Subsetting via an image window or bounding box and selected bands
37:   * Reading of samples into separate arrays or a single pixel-interleaved array
38:   * Configurable tile/strip cache
39:   * Configurable Pool of workers to increase decoding efficiency
40:   * Utility functions for geospatial parameters (Bounding Box, Origin, Resolution)
41:   * Limited [bigTIFF](http://bigtiff.org/#FILE_FORMAT) support
42:   * Automated testing via PhantomJS
43: 
44: Further documentation can be found [here](https://geotiffjs.github.io/geotiff.js/).
45: 
46: ## Example Usage
47: 
48: Geotiff gives you access to all GeoTIFF metadata, but does not offer any one specific higher level API (such as GDAL) for things like transforms or data extraction. However, you can write your own higher level API using this library, given your specific dataset needs.
49: 
50: As an example, here is how you would resolve GPS coordinates to elevation in a GeoTIFF that encodes WGS-84 compliant geo data:
51: 
52: ```js
53: import { fromUrl, fromArrayBuffer, fromBlob  } from "geotiff";
54: 
55: const lerp = (a, b, t) => (1 - t) * a + t * b;
56: 
57: function transform(a, b, M, roundToInt = false) {
58:   const round = (v) => (roundToInt ? v | 0 : v);
59:   return [
60:     round(M[0] + M[1] * a + M[2] * b),
61:     round(M[3] + M[4] * a + M[5] * b),
62:   ];
63: }
64: 
65: // Load our data tile from url, arraybuffer, or blob, so we can work with it:
66: const tiff = await fromArrayBuffer(...);
67: const image = await tiff.getImage(); // by default, the first image is read.
68: 
69: // Construct the WGS-84 forward and inverse affine matrices:
70: const s = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelPixelScale');
71: const t = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelTiepoint');
72: let [sx, sy, sz] = s;
73: let [px, py, k, gx, gy, gz] = t;
74: sy = -sy; // WGS-84 tiles have a "flipped" y component
75: 
76: const pixelToGPS = [gx, sx, 0, gy, 0, sy];
77: console.log(`pixel to GPS transform matrix:`, pixelToGPS);
78: 
79: const gpsToPixel = [-gx / sx, 1 / sx, 0, -gy / sy, 0, 1 / sy];
80: console.log(`GPS to pixel transform matrix:`, gpsToPixel);
81: 
82: // Convert a GPS coordinate to a pixel coordinate in our tile:
83: const [gx1, gy1, gx2, gy2] = image.getBoundingBox();
84: const lat = lerp(gy1, gy2, Math.random());
85: const long = lerp(gx1, gx2, Math.random());
86: console.log(`Looking up GPS coordinate (${lat.toFixed(6)},${long.toFixed(6)})`);
87: 
88: const [x, y] = transform(long, lat, gpsToPixel, true);
89: console.log(`Corresponding tile pixel coordinate: [${x}][${y}]`);
90: 
91: // And as each pixel in the tile covers a geographic area, not a single
92: // GPS coordinate, get the area that this pixel covers:
93: const gpsBBox = [transform(x, y, pixelToGPS), transform(x + 1, y + 1, pixelToGPS)];
94: console.log(`Pixel covers the following GPS area:`, gpsBBox);
95: 
96: // Finally, retrieve the elevation associated with this pixel's geographic area:
97: const rasters = await image.readRasters();
98: const { width, [0]: raster } = rasters;
99: const elevation = raster[x + y * width];
100: console.log(`The elevation at (${lat.toFixed(6)},${long.toFixed(6)}) is ${elevation}m`);
101: ```

115: ## Migration Guide (v2 to v3)
116: 
117: Version 3.0 introduces significant performance improvements through deferred tag reading, but includes breaking changes to some APIs. This guide will help you migrate your code.
118: 
119: ### Summary of Changes
120: 
121: **For most users**: Minimal changes required. The high-level APIs (`getImage()`, `readRasters()`, etc.) remain compatible. You'll mainly need to:
122: - Add `await` to `getTiePoints()` and `getGDALMetadata()`
123: - Change `image.geoKeys` to `image.getGeoKeys()`
124: 
125: **For advanced users**: If you directly access `fileDirectory` properties, you'll need to migrate to the new `ImageFileDirectory` methods.
126: 
127: ### Breaking Changes
128: 
129: #### 1. GeoKeys Access
130: 
131: **Before (v2)**:
132: ```javascript
133: const image = await tiff.getImage();
134: const geoKeys = image.geoKeys;
135: ```
136: 
137: **After (v3)**:
138: ```javascript
139: const image = await tiff.getImage();
140: const geoKeys = image.getGeoKeys();
141: ```
142: 
143: #### 2. getTiePoints() and getGDALMetadata() are now async
144: 
145: **Before (v2)**:
146: ```javascript
147: const tiePoints = image.getTiePoints();
148: const metadata = image.getGDALMetadata();
149: ```
150: 
151: **After (v3)**:
152: ```javascript
153: const tiePoints = await image.getTiePoints();
154: const metadata = await image.getGDALMetadata();
155: ```
156: 
157: #### 3. Accessing fileDirectory properties
158: 
159: The `fileDirectory` object has been replaced with an `ImageFileDirectory` class that supports deferred loading.
160: 
161: **Before (v2)**:
162: ```javascript
163: const image = await tiff.getImage();
164: const { ModelPixelScale: s, ModelTiepoint: t } = image.fileDirectory;
165: const width = image.fileDirectory.ImageWidth;
166: const compression = image.fileDirectory.Compression;
167: ```
168: 
169: **After (v3)** - Use `getValue()` for synchronous access:
170: ```javascript
171: const image = await tiff.getImage();
172: const s = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelPixelScale');
173: const t = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelTiepoint');
174: const width = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ImageWidth');
175: const compression = image.fileDirectory.getValue('Compression');
176: ```
177: 
178: **Note**: `getValue()` throws an error if the tag is deferred. For tags that might be deferred (like large arrays), use `loadValue()`:
179: 
180: ```javascript
181: const colorMap = await image.fileDirectory.loadValue('ColorMap');
182: ```
183: 
184: #### 4. Checking if tags exist
185: 
186: **Before (v2)**:
187: ```javascript
188: if (image.fileDirectory.ModelTiepoint) {
189:   // ...
190: }
191: ```
192: 
193: **After (v3)**:
194: ```javascript
195: if (image.fileDirectory.hasTag('ModelTiepoint')) {
196:   // ...
197: }
198: ```
199: 
200: #### 5. Accessing array elements
201: 
202: For large arrays (like `TileOffsets`, `StripOffsets`), individual elements can now be loaded on-demand:
203: 
204: **Before (v2)**:
205: ```javascript
206: const offset = image.fileDirectory.TileOffsets[5];
207: ```
208: 
209: **After (v3)**:
210: ```javascript
211: const offset = await image.fileDirectory.loadValueIndexed('TileOffsets', 5);
212: ```
213: 
214: #### 6. Pool API changes
215: 
216: If you're using the `Pool` class directly (most users don't):
217: 
218: **Before (v2)**:
219: ```javascript
220: const pool = new GeoTIFF.Pool();
221: const decoded = await pool.decode(fileDirectory, buffer);
222: ```
223: 
224: **After (v3)**:
225: ```javascript
226: const pool = new GeoTIFF.Pool();
227: const compression = fileDirectory.getValue('Compression');
228: const params = await getDecoderParameters(compression, fileDirectory);
229: const boundPool = pool.bindParameters(compression, params);
230: const decoded = await boundPool.decode(buffer);
231: ```
232: 
233: **Note**: When using `readRasters({ pool })`, this is handled automatically.
234: 
235: #### 7. Custom Decoders
236: 
237: If you've implemented custom decoders:
238: 
239: **Before (v2)**:
240: ```javascript
241: class MyDecoder extends BaseDecoder {
242:   async decode(fileDirectory, buffer) {
243:     // decode using fileDirectory properties
244:   }
245: }
246: ```
247: 
248: **After (v3)**:
249: ```javascript
250: class MyDecoder extends BaseDecoder {
251:   constructor(parameters) {
252:     super(parameters);
253:     // parameters extracted once during construction
254:   }
255: 
256:   async decode(buffer) {
257:     // decode using this.parameters
258:   }
259: }
260: 
261: // Register with parameter extraction function
262: addDecoder(
263:   12345, // compression ID
264:   () => import('./mydecoder.js').then(m => m.default),
265:   async (fileDirectory) => {
266:     return {
267:       ...await defaultDecoderParameterFn(fileDirectory),
268:       myCustomParam: await fileDirectory.loadValue('MyCustomTag')
269:     };
270:   }
271: );
272: ```
273: 
274: ### Migration Examples
275: 
276: #### Example 1: Reading with ModelTiepoint/ModelPixelScale
277: 
278: **Before (v2)**:
279: ```javascript
280: const tiff = await fromUrl(url);
281: const image = await tiff.getImage();
282: const { ModelPixelScale: s, ModelTiepoint: t } = image.fileDirectory;
283: const [sx, sy, sz] = s;
284: const [px, py, k, gx, gy, gz] = t;
285: ```
286: 
287: **After (v3)**:
288: ```javascript
289: const tiff = await fromUrl(url);
290: const image = await tiff.getImage();
291: const s = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelPixelScale');
292: const t = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelTiepoint');
293: const [sx, sy, sz] = s;
294: const [px, py, k, gx, gy, gz] = t;
295: ```
296: 
297: #### Example 2: Working with ColorMap (potentially deferred)
298: 
299: **Before (v2)**:
300: ```javascript
301: const image = await tiff.getImage();
302: const colorMap = image.fileDirectory.ColorMap;
303: ```
304: 
305: **After (v3)**:
306: ```javascript
307: const image = await tiff.getImage();
308: const colorMap = await image.fileDirectory.loadValue('ColorMap');
309: ```
310: 
311: #### Example 3: Checking PhotometricInterpretation
312: 
313: **Before (v2)**:
314: ```javascript
315: const pi = image.fileDirectory.PhotometricInterpretation;
316: if (pi === photometricInterpretations.RGB) {
317:   // ...
318: }
319: ```
320: 
321: **After (v3)**:
322: ```javascript
323: const pi = image.fileDirectory.getValue('PhotometricInterpretation');
324: if (pi === photometricInterpretations.RGB) {
325:   // ...
326: }
327: ```
328: 
329: ### What Hasn't Changed
330: 
331: These APIs remain fully backwards compatible:
332: 
333: ```javascript
334: // GeoTIFF class
335: const tiff = await fromUrl(url);
336: const tiff = await fromArrayBuffer(buffer);
337: const tiff = await fromBlob(blob);
338: const imageCount = await tiff.getImageCount();
339: const image = await tiff.getImage(index);
340: 
341: // GeoTIFFImage class
342: const width = image.getWidth();
343: const height = image.getHeight();
344: const samplesPerPixel = image.getSamplesPerPixel();
345: const tileWidth = image.getTileWidth();
346: const tileHeight = image.getTileHeight();
347: const origin = image.getOrigin();
348: const resolution = image.getResolution();
349: const bbox = image.getBoundingBox();
350: 
351: // Reading raster data
352: const data = await image.readRasters({ window, samples, interleave, pool });
353: const rgb = await image.readRGB({ window });
354: 
355: // Writing GeoTIFFs
356: const arrayBuffer = await writeArrayBuffer(values, metadata);
357: ```
358: 
359: ### Performance Benefits
360: 
361: The new deferred loading system provides significant performance improvements:
362: 
363: - **Faster initial parsing**: Large arrays (like tile offsets) are not loaded upfront
364: - **Reduced memory usage**: Only load the data you actually need
365: - **On-demand array access**: Access individual array elements without loading the entire array
366: - **Backward compatible caching**: Frequently accessed tags are eagerly loaded by default

427: ## Install
428: 
429: You can install geotiff.js using npm:
430: ```
431: npm install geotiff
432: ```
433: 
434: or you can use the prebuilt version with a CDN:
435: 
436: ```html
437: <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/geotiff"></script>
438: ```
439: 
440: ## Usage
441: 
442: geotiff.js works with both `require`, `import` and the global variable `GeoTIFF`:
443: 
444: ```javascript
445: const GeoTIFF = require('geotiff');
446: const { fromUrl, fromUrls, fromArrayBuffer, fromBlob } = GeoTIFF;
447: 
448: // or
449: import GeoTIFF, { fromUrl, fromUrls, fromArrayBuffer, fromBlob } from 'geotiff';
450: ```
451: 
452: or:
453: 
454: ```html
455: <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/geotiff"></script>
456: <script>
457:   console.log(GeoTIFF);
458: </script>
459: ```
460: 
461: To parse a GeoTIFF, first a data source is required. To help with the development,
462: there are shortcuts available. The following creates a source that reads from a
463: remote GeoTIFF referenced by a URL:
464: 
465: ```javascript
466: fromUrl(someUrl)
467:   .then(tiff => { /* ... */});
468: 
469: // or when using async/await
470: (async function() {
471:   const tiff = await fromUrl(someUrl);
472:   // ...
473: })()
474: ```
475: 
476: Note: the interactions with geotiff.js objects are oftentimes asynchronous. For
477: the sake of brevity we will only show the async/await syntax and not the
478: `Promise` based one in the following examples.
479: 
480: Accessing remote images is just one way to open TIFF images with geotiff.js. Other
481: options are reading from a local `ArrayBuffer`:
482: 
483: ```javascript
484: // using local ArrayBuffer
485: const response = await fetch(someUrl);
486: const arrayBuffer = await response.arrayBuffer();
487: const tiff = await fromArrayBuffer(arrayBuffer);
488: ```
489: 
490: or a `Blob`/`File`:
491: 
492: ```html
493: <input type="file" id="file">
494: <script>
495:   const input = document.getElementById('file');
496:   input.onchange = async function() {
497:     const tiff = await fromBlob(input.files[0]);
498:   }
499: </script>
500: ```
501: 
502: Now that we have opened the TIFF file, we can inspect it. The TIFF is structured
503: in a small header and a list of one or more images (Image File Directory, IFD to
504: use the TIFF nomenclature). To get one image by index the `getImage()` function
505: must be used. This is again an asynchronous operation, as the IFDs are loaded
506: lazily:
507: 
508: ```javascript
509: const image = await tiff.getImage(); // by default, the first image is read.
510: ```
511: 
512: Now that we have obtained a `GeoTIFFImage` object we can inspect its metadata
513: (like size, tiling, number of samples, geographical information, etc.). All
514: the metadata is parsed once the IFD is first parsed, thus the access to that
515: is synchronous:
516: 
517: ```javascript
518: const width = image.getWidth();
519: const height = image.getHeight();
520: const tileWidth = image.getTileWidth();
521: const tileHeight = image.getTileHeight();
522: const samplesPerPixel = image.getSamplesPerPixel();
523: 
524: // when we are actually dealing with geo-data the following methods return
525: // meaningful results:
526: const origin = image.getOrigin();
527: const resolution = image.getResolution();
528: const bbox = image.getBoundingBox();
529: ```
530: 
531: The actual raster data is not fetched and parsed automatically. This is because
532: it is usually much more spacious and the decoding of the pixels can be time
533: consuming due to the necessity of decompression.
534: 
535: To read a whole image into one big array of arrays the following method call can be used:
536: 
537: ```javascript
538: const data = await image.readRasters();
539: ```
540: 
541: For convenience the result always has a `width` and `height` attribute:
542: 
543: ```javascript
544: const data = await image.readRasters();
545: const { width, height } = data;
546: ```
547: 
548: By default, the raster is split to a separate array for each component. For an RGB image
549: for example, we'd get three arrays, one for red, green and blue.
550: 
551: ```javascript
552: const [red, green, blue] = await image.readRasters();
553: ```
554: 
555: If we want instead all the bands interleaved in one big array, we have to pass the
556: `interleave: true` option:
557: 
558: ```javascript
559: const [r0, g0, b0, r1, g1, b1, ...] = await image.readRasters({ interleave: true });
560: ```
561: 
562: If we are only interested in a specific region of the image, the `window` option can be
563: used to limit reading in that bounding box. Note: the bounding box is in 'image coordinates'
564: not geographical ones:
565: 
566: ```javascript
567: const left = 50;
568: const top = 10;
569: const right = 150;
570: const bottom = 60;
571: 
572: const data = await image.readRasters({ window: [left, top, right, bottom] });
573: ```
574: 
575: This image window can go beyond the image bounds. In that case it might be usefull to supply
576: a `fillValue: value` option (can also be an array, one value for each sample).
577: 
578: It is also possible to just read specific samples for each pixel. For example, we can only
579: read the red component from an RGB image:
580: 
581: ```javascript
582: const [red] = await image.readRasters({ samples: [0] });
583: ```
584: 
585: When you want your output in a specific size, you can use the `width` and `height` options.
586: This defaults of course to the size of your supplied `window` or the image size if no
587: `window` was supplied.
588: 
589: As the data now needs to be resampled, a `resampleMethod` can be specified. This defaults to
590: the nearest neighbour method, but also the `'bilinear'` method is supported:
591: 
592: ```javascript
593: const data = await image.readRasters({ width: 40, height: 40, resampleMethod: 'bilinear' });
594: ```
595: 
596: ### Using decoder pools to improve parsing performance
597: 
598: Decoding compressed images can be a time consuming process. To minimize this
599: geotiff.js provides the `Pool` mechanism which uses WebWorkers to split the amount
600: of work on multiple 'threads'.
601: 
602: ```javascript
603: const pool = new GeoTIFF.Pool();
604: const data = await image.readRasters({ pool });
605: ```
606: 
607: It is possible to provide a pool size (i.e: number of workers), by default the number
608: of available processors is used.
609: 
610: ### Dealing with visual data
611: 
612: The TIFF specification provides various ways to encode visual data. In the
613: specification this is called photometric interpretation. The simplest case we
614: already dealt with is the RGB one. Others are grayscale, paletted images, CMYK,
615: YCbCr, and CIE L*a*b.
616: 
617: geotiff.js provides a method to automatically convert these images to RGB:
618: `readRGB()`. This method is very similar to the `readRasters` method with
619: the distinction that the `interleave` option now defaults to `true` and the
620: `samples` are automatically chosen.
621: 
622: ```javascript
623: const rgb = await image.readRGB({
624:   // options...
625: });
626: ```
627: 
628: ### Automatic image selection (experimental)
629: 
630: When dealing with images that have internal (or even external, see the next section)
631: overviews, `GeoTIFF` objects provide a separate `readRasters` method. This method
632: works very similar to the method on the `GeoTIFFImage` objects with the same name.
633: By default, it uses the larges image available (highest resolution), but when either
634: `width`, `height`, `resX`, or `resY` are specified, then the best fitting image will
635: be used for reading.
636: 
637: Additionally, it allows the `bbox` instead of the `window` parameter. This works
638: similarly, but uses geographic coordinates instead of pixel ones.
639: 
640: ```javascript
641: const data = await tiff.readRasters({
642:   bbox: [10.34, 57.28, 13.34, 60.23],
643:   resX: 0.1,
644:   resY: 0.1
645: });
646: ```
647: 
648: ### External overviews
649: 
650: Especially for certain kinds of high resolution images it is not uncommon to separate
651: the highest resolution from the lower resolution overviews (usually using the `.ovr`
652: extension). With geotiff.js it is possible to use files of this setup, just as you
653: would use single-file images by taking advantage of the `MultiGeoTIFF` objects. They
654: behave exactly the same as the before mentioned `GeoTIFF` objects: you can select
655: images by index or read data using `readRasters`. Toget such a file use the `fromUrls`
656: factory function:
657: 
658: ```javascript
659: const multiTiff = await fromUrls(
660:   'LC08_L1TP_189027_20170403_20170414_01_T1_B3.TIF',
661:   ['LC08_L1TP_189027_20170403_20170414_01_T1_B3.TIF.ovr']
662: );
663: ```
664: 
665: ### AbortController Support
666: 
667: Geotiff.js supports the use of [`AbortController`s](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortController). Calls to `getRasters`, `readRGB` and `getTileOrStrip` will throw an `Error` with name `AbortSignal` similar to the browser's `fetch` behavior.
668: 
669: ```javascript
670: const tiff = await fromUrl(source);
671: const abortController = new AbortController();
672: const { signal } = abortController;
673: abortController.abort();
674: try {
675:   const data = await tiff.readRasters({ signal });
676: } catch(e) {
677:   if (err.name === 'AbortError') {
678:     // do stuff
679:   }
680: }
681: ```
682: 
683: ### Writing GeoTIFFs (Beta Version)
684: 
685: You can create a binary representation of a GeoTIFF using `writeArrayBuffer`.
686: This function returns an ArrayBuffer which you can then save as a .tif file.
687: :warning: writeArrayBuffer currently writes the values uncompressed
688: ```javascript
689: import GeoTIFF, { writeArrayBuffer } from 'geotiff';
690: 
691: const values = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9];
692: const metadata = {
693:   height: 3,
694:   width: 3
695: };
696: const arrayBuffer = await writeArrayBuffer(values, metadata);
697: ```
698: 
699: You can also customize the metadata using names found in the [TIFF Spec](https://www.loc.gov/preservation/digital/formats/content/tiff_tags.shtml) and [GeoTIFF spec](https://cdn.earthdata.nasa.gov/conduit/upload/6852/geotiff-1.8.1-1995-10-31.pdf).
700: ```javascript
701: import { writeArrayBuffer } from 'geotiff';
702: 
703: const values = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9];
704: const metadata = {
705:   GeographicTypeGeoKey: 4326,
706:   height: 3,
707:   ModelPixelScale: [0.031355, 0.031355, 0],
708:   ModelTiepoint: [0, 0, 0, 11.331755000000001, 46.268645, 0],
709:   width: 3
710: };
711: const arrayBuffer = await writeArrayBuffer(values, metadata);
712: ```
713: 
714: To write geotiffs with multiple strips by specifying the metadata for `StripByteCounts` and `RowsPerStrip`:
715: ```javascript
716: const originalRed = [
717:     [255, 255, 255],
718:     [0, 0, 0],
719:     [0, 0, 0],
720: ];
721: const originalGreen = [
722:   [0, 0, 0],
723:   [255, 255, 255],
724:   [0, 0, 0],
725: ];
726: const originalBlue = [
727:   [0, 0, 0],
728:   [0, 0, 0],
729:   [255, 255, 255],
730: ];
731: const interleaved = originalRed.flatMap((row, rowIdx) => row.flatMap((value, colIdx) => [
732:   value, originalGreen[rowIdx][colIdx], originalBlue[rowIdx][colIdx],
733: ]));
734: const values = new Uint8Array(interleaved);
735: const metadata = {
736:   height: 3,
737:   width: 3,
738:   RowsPerStrip: 1,
739:   StripByteCounts: [9, 9, 9],
740: };
741: 
742: const newGeoTiffAsBinaryData = await writeArrayBuffer(values, metadata);
743: ```
744: 
745: To create tiled geotiffs, specify the metadata for: `TileByteCounts`, `TileWidth`, `TileLength` and `SamplesPerPixel`:
746: ```javascript
747: const originalRed = [
748:     [255, 255, 255],
749:     [1, 1, 1],
750:     [1, 1, 1],
751: ];
752: const originalGreen = [
753:   [1, 1, 1],
754:   [255, 255, 255],
755:   [1, 1, 1],
756: ];
757: const originalBlue = [
758:   [1, 1, 1],
759:   [1, 1, 1],
760:   [255, 255, 255],
761: ];
762: 
763: const tileHeight = 2;
764: const tileWidth = 2;
765: const height = 3;
766: const width = 3;
767: const samplesPerPixel = 3;
768: 
769: // You must provide your own flattenAndPadTiledDataInterleaved implementation, bear in mind partial tiles must be padded with null bytes
770: const tiled = flattenAndPadTiledDataInterleaved(interleaved, width, height, tileWidth, tileHeight, samplesPerPixel);
771: const metadata = {
772:   height,
773:   width,
774:   TileByteCounts: [12, 12, 12, 12],
775:   TileWidth: tileWidth,
776:   TileLength: tileHeight,
777:   SamplesPerPixel: samplesPerPixel,
778: };
779: ```
780: 
781: ## What to do with the data?
782: 
783: There is a nice HTML 5/WebGL based rendering library called
784: [plotty](https://github.com/santilland/plotty), that allows for some really nice
785: on the fly rendering of the data contained in a GeoTIFF.
786: 
787: ```html
788: <canvas id="plot"></canvas>
789: <script>
790:   // ...
791: 
792:   (async function() {
793:     const tiff = await fromUrl(url);
794:     const image = await tiff.getImage();
795:     const data = await image.readRasters();
796: 
797:     const canvas = document.getElementById("plot");
798:     const plot = new plotty.plot({
799:       canvas,
800:       data: data[0],
801:       width: image.getWidth(),
802:       height: image.getHeight(),
803:       domain: [0, 256],
804:       colorScale: "viridis"
805:     });
806:     plot.render();
807:   })();
808: </script>
809: ```
810: 
811: There's also a library called [geotiff-geokeys-to-proj4](https://github.com/matafokka/geotiff-geokeys-to-proj4), that allows for reprojecting pixel coordinates and, therefore, consuming geospatial data contained in GeoTIFF.
812: 
813: ## BigTIFF support
814: 
815: geotiff.js has a limited support for files in the BigTIFF format. The limitations
816: originate in the capabilities of current JavaScript implementations regarding
817: 64 bit integer parsers and structures: there are no functions to read 64 bit
818: integers from a stream and no such typed arrays. As BigTIFF relies on 64 bit
819: offsets and also allows tag values of those types. In order to still provide
820: a reasonable support, the following is implemented:
821: 
822:   * 64 bit integers are read as two 32 bit integers and then combined. As
823:     numbers in JavaScript are typically implemented as 64 bit floats, there
824:     might be inaccuracies for *very* large values.
825:   * For 64 bit integer arrays, the default `Array` type is used. This might
826:     cause problems for some compression algorithms if those arrays are used for
827:     pixel values.
828: 
829: ## n-bit Support
830: 
831: geotiff.js has some n-bit support which means that it supports unsigned integer
832: data reading with each element using a non-multiple of 8 bit depth. This only
833: works with band interleaved images (see
834: [this related issue](https://github.com/geotiffjs/geotiff.js/issues/202)).
835:

Read (geospatial) metadata and raw array data from a wide variety of different
(Geo)TIFF files types.

## Features

Currently available functionality:

  * Parsing TIFFs from various sources:
    * remote (via `fetch` or XHR)
    * from a local `ArrayBuffer`
    * from the filesystem (on Browsers using the `FileReader` and on node using the filesystem functions)
  * Parsing the headers of all possible TIFF files
  * Rudimentary extraction of geospatial metadata
  * Reading raster data from:
    * stripped images
    * tiled images
    * band interleaved images
    * pixel interleaved images
  * Supported data-types:
    * (U)Int8/16/32
    * UInt1-31 (with some drawbacks)
    * Float16/32/64
  * Enabled compressions:
    * no compression
    * Packbits
    * LZW
    * Deflate (with floating point or horizontal predictor support)
    * JPEG
    * LERC (with additional Deflate compression support)
    * Zstandard
    * image formats supported via the browser (such as WebP)
  * Automatic selection of overview level to read from
  * Subsetting via an image window or bounding box and selected bands
  * Reading of samples into separate arrays or a single pixel-interleaved array
  * Configurable tile/strip cache
  * Configurable Pool of workers to increase decoding efficiency
  * Utility functions for geospatial parameters (Bounding Box, Origin, Resolution)
  * Limited [bigTIFF](http://bigtiff.org/#FILE_FORMAT) support
  * Automated testing via PhantomJS

Further documentation can be found [here](https://geotiffjs.github.io/geotiff.js/).

## Example Usage

Geotiff gives you access to all GeoTIFF metadata, but does not offer any one specific higher level API (such as GDAL) for things like transforms or data extraction. However, you can write your own higher level API using this library, given your specific dataset needs.

As an example, here is how you would resolve GPS coordinates to elevation in a GeoTIFF that encodes WGS-84 compliant geo data:

```js
import { fromUrl, fromArrayBuffer, fromBlob  } from "geotiff";

const lerp = (a, b, t) => (1 - t) * a + t * b;

function transform(a, b, M, roundToInt = false) {
  const round = (v) => (roundToInt ? v | 0 : v);
  return [
    round(M[0] + M[1] * a + M[2] * b),
    round(M[3] + M[4] * a + M[5] * b),
  ];
}

// Load our data tile from url, arraybuffer, or blob, so we can work with it:
const tiff = await fromArrayBuffer(...);
const image = await tiff.getImage(); // by default, the first image is read.

// Construct the WGS-84 forward and inverse affine matrices:
const s = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelPixelScale');
const t = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelTiepoint');
let [sx, sy, sz] = s;
let [px, py, k, gx, gy, gz] = t;
sy = -sy; // WGS-84 tiles have a "flipped" y component

const pixelToGPS = [gx, sx, 0, gy, 0, sy];
console.log(`pixel to GPS transform matrix:`, pixelToGPS);

const gpsToPixel = [-gx / sx, 1 / sx, 0, -gy / sy, 0, 1 / sy];
console.log(`GPS to pixel transform matrix:`, gpsToPixel);

// Convert a GPS coordinate to a pixel coordinate in our tile:
const [gx1, gy1, gx2, gy2] = image.getBoundingBox();
const lat = lerp(gy1, gy2, Math.random());
const long = lerp(gx1, gx2, Math.random());
console.log(`Looking up GPS coordinate (${lat.toFixed(6)},${long.toFixed(6)})`);

const [x, y] = transform(long, lat, gpsToPixel, true);
console.log(`Corresponding tile pixel coordinate: [${x}][${y}]`);

// And as each pixel in the tile covers a geographic area, not a single
// GPS coordinate, get the area that this pixel covers:
const gpsBBox = [transform(x, y, pixelToGPS), transform(x + 1, y + 1, pixelToGPS)];
console.log(`Pixel covers the following GPS area:`, gpsBBox);

// Finally, retrieve the elevation associated with this pixel's geographic area:
const rasters = await image.readRasters();
const { width, [0]: raster } = rasters;
const elevation = raster[x + y * width];
console.log(`The elevation at (${lat.toFixed(6)},${long.toFixed(6)}) is ${elevation}m`);
```

## Migration Guide (v2 to v3)

Version 3.0 introduces significant performance improvements through deferred tag reading, but includes breaking changes to some APIs. This guide will help you migrate your code.

### Summary of Changes

**For most users**: Minimal changes required. The high-level APIs (`getImage()`, `readRasters()`, etc.) remain compatible. You'll mainly need to:
- Add `await` to `getTiePoints()` and `getGDALMetadata()`
- Change `image.geoKeys` to `image.getGeoKeys()`

**For advanced users**: If you directly access `fileDirectory` properties, you'll need to migrate to the new `ImageFileDirectory` methods.

### Breaking Changes

#### 1. GeoKeys Access

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const geoKeys = image.geoKeys;
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const geoKeys = image.getGeoKeys();
```

#### 2. getTiePoints() and getGDALMetadata() are now async

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const tiePoints = image.getTiePoints();
const metadata = image.getGDALMetadata();
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
const tiePoints = await image.getTiePoints();
const metadata = await image.getGDALMetadata();
```

#### 3. Accessing fileDirectory properties

The `fileDirectory` object has been replaced with an `ImageFileDirectory` class that supports deferred loading.

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const { ModelPixelScale: s, ModelTiepoint: t } = image.fileDirectory;
const width = image.fileDirectory.ImageWidth;
const compression = image.fileDirectory.Compression;
```

**After (v3)** - Use `getValue()` for synchronous access:
```javascript
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const s = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelPixelScale');
const t = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelTiepoint');
const width = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ImageWidth');
const compression = image.fileDirectory.getValue('Compression');
```

**Note**: `getValue()` throws an error if the tag is deferred. For tags that might be deferred (like large arrays), use `loadValue()`:

```javascript
const colorMap = await image.fileDirectory.loadValue('ColorMap');
```

#### 4. Checking if tags exist

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
if (image.fileDirectory.ModelTiepoint) {
  // ...
}
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
if (image.fileDirectory.hasTag('ModelTiepoint')) {
  // ...
}
```

#### 5. Accessing array elements

For large arrays (like `TileOffsets`, `StripOffsets`), individual elements can now be loaded on-demand:

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const offset = image.fileDirectory.TileOffsets[5];
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
const offset = await image.fileDirectory.loadValueIndexed('TileOffsets', 5);
```

#### 6. Pool API changes

If you're using the `Pool` class directly (most users don't):

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const pool = new GeoTIFF.Pool();
const decoded = await pool.decode(fileDirectory, buffer);
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
const pool = new GeoTIFF.Pool();
const compression = fileDirectory.getValue('Compression');
const params = await getDecoderParameters(compression, fileDirectory);
const boundPool = pool.bindParameters(compression, params);
const decoded = await boundPool.decode(buffer);
```

**Note**: When using `readRasters({ pool })`, this is handled automatically.

#### 7. Custom Decoders

If you've implemented custom decoders:

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
class MyDecoder extends BaseDecoder {
  async decode(fileDirectory, buffer) {
    // decode using fileDirectory properties
  }
}
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
class MyDecoder extends BaseDecoder {
  constructor(parameters) {
    super(parameters);
    // parameters extracted once during construction
  }

  async decode(buffer) {
    // decode using this.parameters
  }
}

// Register with parameter extraction function
addDecoder(
  12345, // compression ID
  () => import('./mydecoder.js').then(m => m.default),
  async (fileDirectory) => {
    return {
      ...await defaultDecoderParameterFn(fileDirectory),
      myCustomParam: await fileDirectory.loadValue('MyCustomTag')
    };
  }
);
```

### Migration Examples

#### Example 1: Reading with ModelTiepoint/ModelPixelScale

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const tiff = await fromUrl(url);
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const { ModelPixelScale: s, ModelTiepoint: t } = image.fileDirectory;
const [sx, sy, sz] = s;
const [px, py, k, gx, gy, gz] = t;
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
const tiff = await fromUrl(url);
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const s = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelPixelScale');
const t = image.fileDirectory.getValue('ModelTiepoint');
const [sx, sy, sz] = s;
const [px, py, k, gx, gy, gz] = t;
```

#### Example 2: Working with ColorMap (potentially deferred)

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const colorMap = image.fileDirectory.ColorMap;
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
const image = await tiff.getImage();
const colorMap = await image.fileDirectory.loadValue('ColorMap');
```

#### Example 3: Checking PhotometricInterpretation

**Before (v2)**:
```javascript
const pi = image.fileDirectory.PhotometricInterpretation;
if (pi === photometricInterpretations.RGB) {
  // ...
}
```

**After (v3)**:
```javascript
const pi = image.fileDirectory.getValue('PhotometricInterpretation');
if (pi === photometricInterpretations.RGB) {
  // ...
}
```

### What Hasn't Changed

These APIs remain fully backwards compatible:

```javascript
// GeoTIFF class
const tiff = await fromUrl(url);
const tiff = await fromArrayBuffer(buffer);
const tiff = await fromBlob(blob);
const imageCount = await tiff.getImageCount();
const image = await tiff.getImage(index);

// GeoTIFFImage class
const width = image.getWidth();
const height = image.getHeight();
const samplesPerPixel = image.getSamplesPerPixel();
const tileWidth = image.getTileWidth();
const tileHeight = image.getTileHeight();
const origin = image.getOrigin();
const resolution = image.getResolution();
const bbox = image.getBoundingBox();

// Reading raster data
const data = await image.readRasters({ window, samples, interleave, pool });
const rgb = await image.readRGB({ window });

// Writing GeoTIFFs
const arrayBuffer = await writeArrayBuffer(values, metadata);
```

### Performance Benefits

The new deferred loading system provides significant performance improvements:

- **Faster initial parsing**: Large arrays (like tile offsets) are not loaded upfront
- **Reduced memory usage**: Only load the data you actually need
- **On-demand array access**: Access individual array elements without loading the entire array
- **Backward compatible caching**: Frequently accessed tags are eagerly loaded by default

## Setup

To setup the repository do the following steps:

```bash
# clone repo
git clone https://github.com/constantinius/geotiff.js.git
cd geotiff.js/

# install development dependencies
npm install
```

## Testing and Building

In order to run the tests you first have to set up the test data. This requires
the [GDAL](http://gdal.org/) and [ImageMagick](http://imagemagick.org/) tools.
Installation of these tools varies according to the operating system, the
following listing shows the installation on Ubuntu (using the ubuntugis-unstable
repository):
```bash
sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:ubuntugis/ubuntugis-unstable
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y gdal-bin imagemagick
```
To install GDAL and ImageMagick on MacOS X, please use [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/). The setup script also needs `wget` on MacOS X
```bash
brew install wget gdal imagemagick
```

When GDAL and ImageMagick is installed, the test data setup script can be run:
```bash
cd test/data
sh setup_data.sh
cd -
```

To test the library (using PhantomJS, karma, mocha and chai) do the following:

```bash
npm test
```

To do some in-browser testing do:

```bash
npm run dev
```

and navigate to `http://localhost:8090/test/`

To build the library do:

```bash
npm run build
```

The output is written to `dist-browser/main.js` and `dist-node/main.js`.

You can install geotiff.js using npm:
```
npm install geotiff
